context: The three suite elements declare tests 12 + 5 + 4 = 21, failures 2, errors 0, skipped 2. The file actually contains 23 testcase elements: 17 passing, 1 failure, 1 error, 4 skipped. web.CheckoutSpec declares failures="2" while its body holds one <failure> and one <error>, and declares skipped="0" while holding two <skipped>. api.OrdersSpec declares tests="5" while holding 7 testcases, its tests count excluding the 2 it reports separately as skipped. api.RefundsSpec's summary is accurate. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads the suite attributes, since they are the only totals in the file and are exactly what a summary line is for, and republishes 21 / 2 / 0 / 2 - the same wrong numbers the gate already publishes, which look authoritative because they came from the report. A second predicted failure is recounting correctly but keeping the vendor's habit of reporting the error inside the failure count. A third is declaring the whole file untrustworthy rather than identifying which suite drifts and in which direction.

checklist.name: Script, tests, and write-up delivered
checklist.description: scripts/verify-report.js runs and writes verified-counts.json, test/verify-report.test.js exists, verified-counts.md exists, and npm test passes with the pre-existing test/xml.test.js still passing.

checklist.name: Totals derived from the testcase elements
checklist.description: The published totals are 23 tests, 17 passed, 1 failure, 1 error, 4 skipped. Publishing 21 tests, or 2 failures, or 0 errors, or 2 skipped - any figure taken from the suite attributes - scores zero. Correct numbers in the prose while verified-counts.json still emits the declared ones scores at most half.

checklist.name: Drift reported per suite and directionally
checklist.description: Both disagreements are named specifically: web.CheckoutSpec declares 12 tests / 2 failures / 0 skipped against a body of 12 testcases, 1 failure, 1 error and 2 skipped; api.OrdersSpec declares 5 tests against 7 testcase elements because its count leaves out the skipped ones. Reporting only that 'the numbers do not match' with no per-suite direction scores at most half; missing either suite scores zero.

checklist.name: Error not folded into failures
checklist.description: MUST NOT reproduce the suite element's habit of counting the error inside failures. 'charges the card' carries an <error> and is reported as an error, separately from the 1 assertion failure. Any published figure of 2 failures with no error count scores zero on this criterion - this is the exact hole the gate fell through.

checklist.name: The accurate suite identified as accurate
checklist.description: api.RefundsSpec is reported as consistent - 4 declared, 4 found, no disagreement. Marking all three suites as untrustworthy scores zero here: a check that flags everything gives the gate nothing to act on.

checklist.name: Executable test covers the recount
checklist.description: test/verify-report.test.js asserts against a fixture whose suite attributes disagree with its testcase elements and proves the derived counts win, and passes. A test built only on a self-consistent fixture scores at most half; no runnable test scores zero.

checklist.name: Authority stated for the future
checklist.description: verified-counts.md states which figures the metrics job should treat as authoritative and why, so this does not have to be re-litigated at the next vendor upgrade. Reporting Friday's numbers only scores at most half.
